question: After an attributable selected-target kill by the first single-target Attack in a player turn, does exactly one unclosed immediately-next-PLAY class among all-enemy Attack, Skill and Power have robust active, exact-inactive, viable, broad-card and closed-family-separated discovery capacity?
hypothesis: The 79 intervening-PLAY aliases in the closed single-target kill relay may contain a broader fight-local causal sequencing unit. Exhaustively classifying the immediate next PLAY tests that finite repertoire without inventing a card subset, payoff variant, policy cohort or simulator row.

closedFamilyExclusions.attackEnemy: The exact direct-kill-to-next-single-target-Attack family is an immutable reproduction control only and cannot be selected or rescued.
closedFamilyExclusions.targetTransfer: The closed target-transfer family requires the first target to survive; this census requires that target to die before the immediate next PLAY.
closedFamilyExclusions.reaperBell: The closed Reaper Bell family is acquisition-bound immediate Energy plus draw on death; it remains a one-sided natural-interference anchor only.
closedFamilyExclusions.scorelineAndAfterimage: Scoreline and Afterimage remain separate closed factors fixed off and are never pooled with this endpoint.
closedFamilyExclusions.otherClosedFamilies: Do not reconstruct Kindle, Ward, Ember-reserve, cadence, focused-to-sweep, action-economy, one-bit setup, heavy relay, same-instance repeat, acquisition scalar, private-debt or historical scalar paths.
closedFamilyExclusions.method: No ML, RL, optimiser, policy remap, grammar expansion or adaptive candidate-by-candidate tuning is permitted.

futureMechanismTemplate.producer: The first authored type=attack,target=enemy PLAY in a multi-enemy player turn is followed by DIE for its exact selected target before the immediate next PLAY.
futureMechanismTemplate.consumer: Exactly one selected immediate-next-PLAY class: authored type=attack,target=allEnemies, type=skill, or type=power. Exact card IDs are breadth witnesses, not candidate levels.
futureMechanismTemplate.mediator: One Dusk-only player-turn-local kill hold consumed by the immediate next PLAY; no RunState or save field.
futureMechanismTemplate.commonPayoff: After the selected consumer resolves, grant exactly one bounded Ember, at most once in that player turn. This common payoff is a later identity-prototype contract only and is not implemented or estimated here.
futureMechanismTemplate.payoffProvenance: One Ember is the smallest positive unit of the existing Dusk fight-local resource and introduces no scalar level.
futureMechanismTemplate.duskBoundary: Existing Emberheart is the proposed Dusk gate; Ashwarden and mechanism-off remain exact current-main paths.
futureMechanismTemplate.acquisition: None; existing content, reward pools, rarities, policies and saves are unchanged.
futureMechanismTemplate.rngAndPersistence: No RNG call or cursor movement, new content ID, reward entry, save field or save version.
futureMechanismTemplate.telemetry: Research-only exact producer PLAY, target DIE, hold set/clear, consumer class/card, consume, payoff and turn expiry.

killConsumerPayoff.definition: The future mechanism template with one selected consumer class and the common one-Ember payoff.
killConsumerPayoff.status: All levels are fixed off here. At most one enabled level may survive this census; the other enabled levels close without prototype.

reaperBellPath.definition: Unmodified current-main natural reward and death path.

frozenCausalFactors.independence: This zero-row census is not a factorial or causal contrast; Scoreline and Afterimage remain separate factors.

identity-proved-current-main-target-deat.status: Sole immutable cached observation arm; deterministic classification adds no simulator row.

design.type: Zero-new-row complete-cohort mutually exclusive consumer-topology census; not a factorial and not a causal experiment.
design.construction: For each multi-enemy player turn, locate the first authored single-target Attack. If its selected target dies before the immediate next PLAY, classify that next PLAY exactly once as attack-enemy, attack-allEnemies, skill, power or unclassified; record no-next-play when absent.
mechanisticallyJustifiedInteractions: First selected-target kill by immediate next PLAY establishes the complete sequencing opportunity.
Producer death by one selected consumer class defines the sole future mediator; neither condition alone is sufficient.
Dusk identity by the selected consumer payoff is the sole future causal interaction and is not estimated here.
design.aliasStructure: attack-enemy is the closed kill-relay reproduction control. no-next-play is an exhausted topology leaf. unclassified is a schema fault. Scoreline and Afterimage are two-sided repertoire anchors; Reaper Bell, target transfer and the closed kill relay are one-sided alias anchors.
design.omittedCells: No exact-card subset, second/third consumer, consumer ordering, payoff value, duration, acquisition, rarity, policy knob, cohort replacement, simulator, held-out, joint package, ML, RL, optimiser or protected-seed cell.

trace.selectionRule: Read all 256 rows once. No row, policy, seed, fight, turn, class, card, threshold, anchor or endpoint is selected after execution.

cohort.identity: Every policy and seed in the complete frozen current-main rectangle is read exactly once; each policy has one exact snapshot across four seeds.

scoreline.status: Immutable two-sided anchor; Scoreline fixed off.

afterimage.status: Immutable two-sided anchor; Afterimage fixed off.

closedControl.role: Exact reconstruction control for attributable direct-kill rows and policy support; never selectable.

estimands.unit: Policy identity over its complete four-seed rectangle.
estimands.active: At least one class-specific immediate post-kill consumer event in at least two of four rows.
estimands.inactive: No class-specific event in any of four rows.
estimands.viable: An active policy with at least one qualifying row that wins.
estimands.breadth: Distinct exact producer cards, consumer cards and ordered producer-consumer pairs.
estimands.separation: Two-sided separation from Scoreline and Afterimage plus one-sided candidate-only separation from Reaper Bell, target transfer and the closed kill relay.
estimands.notEstimated: Payoff identity, causal effect, complementarity, duration, Ash isolation, fresh-cohort reproducibility, held-out confirmation, package admission, detector score, product balance or P9 acceptance.

gates.provenance: The 16-policy active/inactive, eight-policy viability, four-producer, eight-pair, eight-policy separation and 0.55 overlap thresholds reuse the preregistered 64-policy structural-capacity scale. Consumer breadth is class-specific: three of four all-enemy Attacks or four cards for larger classes.

selectionRule.eligible: A class must pass every support, viability, breadth, separation, semantic and reliability gate.

claimBoundary: Discovery-stage immediate-consumer topology, natural policy capacity and closed-family alias separation only; no gameplay implementation, realised payoff, causal, fresh-cohort, held-out, package-admission, detector, product or P9 claim.

decisionRules.success: The closed attack-enemy control reproduces exactly, the complete partition is valid, and at least one candidate passes every frozen gate at the sole look.
decisionRules.successAuthority: Apply boundary 1: freeze at most the first class under the deterministic selection order for a separate exact-null and direct-mediator identity prototype of the common one-Ember contract. The other classes close. Add no causal row before omitted/off path, RNG, result, policy and seed identity plus direct producer, hold, consume, expiry, Ash and scope-isolation controls pass. Then freeze fresh unprotected discovery and independently held-out cohorts before efficacy evidence.
decisionRules.futility: The closed control reproduces and inputs are valid, but no candidate passes every frozen gate.
decisionRules.futilityAuthority: Apply boundary 2: close the complete immediate post-kill consumer topology without exact-card subset, second/third consumer, ordering, payoff, duration, carrier, acquisition, cohort, policy or method rescue; continue with the next evidence-backed minimal structural mechanism inside #421.
decisionRules.inconclusive: An immutable input, source, trace, schema, closed control, ledger or wall-time check prevents the complete deterministic decision.
decisionRules.inconclusiveAuthority: Apply boundary 3: record the exact missing relevant gate at the cap; add no repair, rerun, replacement trace, simulator row, method or protected seed, then follow the current human-authority contract.

order: Verify task, authority, refs, source, helpers, trace identity, closed evidence and ledger.
Reproduce the closed attack-enemy control and classify every qualifying immediate next PLAY once.
Apply all three candidate gate sets once and the deterministic at-most-one selection order.
Verify byte-identical ledger identity and apply exactly one decision boundary.
executionAndStopping.firstLook: The complete 256-row cached rectangle is the sole look; no predicate, class, card subset, threshold, anchor or endpoint may change after execution begins.
executionAndStopping.stagedConstraint: Success can justify only one exact identity prototype. This discovery cohort cannot serve as held-out efficacy evidence.
executionAndStopping.futureCrnConstraint: Any later causal contrast uses the same frozen policy identities, seed identities, baseline, first-look budget, estimator and stopping rule at every compared level.
executionAndStopping.knobIdentityConstraint: Before any future row, omitted and explicit-off settings reproduce exact path, RNG identity and result; deterministic controls prove only the selected mediator and one-Ember payoff change.
executionAndStopping.methodConstraint: Deterministic code owns construction, caching, fitting and stop/go. No ML, RL or optimiser unless a later comparable experiment identifies a remaining repertoire bottleneck and measures decision value.
executionAndStopping.stopping: One zero-row complete-cohort look; exactly one of success, futility or inconclusive. No peeking, threshold relaxation, subset rescue, cohort replacement or endpoint addition.
